grammar_concept.title: Passive Voice: be + past participle
grammar_concept.rule: Use the passive voice (be + past participle) when the action is more important than who did it, or when we don't know or don't need to say who did it: "The report was written yesterday" (we don't say by whom).
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Na voz passiva, o foco passa da pessoa que faz a ação para a coisa que recebe a ação. O sujeito da frase deixa de ser quem faz, passa a ser quem sofre a ação.
grammar_concept.example: The email was sent this morning. This building was built in 1990.
grammar_concept.example_translation: O email foi enviado esta manhã. Este edifício foi construído em 1990.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português, além da voz passiva com "ser" + particípio (semelhante ao inglês), é muito comum usar-se a construção reflexiva ("constrói-se", "vende-se") para o mesmo efeito — isto não existe em inglês, o que leva alguns falantes de português a esquecer o verbo "be" na passiva inglesa: dizem "The building built in 1990" em vez de "The building was built in 1990".
grammar_concept.correction: A passiva em inglês precisa sempre do verbo "be" (no tempo certo) + particípio passado: is/are/was/were/has been + particípio. Nunca se omite o "be". Para dizer quem fez a ação (opcional), usa-se "by": "The email was sent by Sarah."
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Num relatório formal: "The results were analysed and the data was presented at the meeting."

vocabulary.definition_en: to examine something carefully in order to understand it
example_sentences: The results were analysed by the research team.

vocabulary.definition_en: to prepare and issue a book, report or other written material for the public
example_sentences: The report will be published next month.
These cars are produced in Germany.

exercises.explanation: O foco é o edifício (não quem construiu), e a ação aconteceu no passado → Past Simple passivo: was + particípio.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Esquecer o "was" ("This building built in 1990") é o erro mais comum.

correct_answer: The email was sent this morning.
distractors: The email was send this morning.
The email is sent this morning already.
exercises.explanation: "Was sent" é a forma correta: was + particípio passado ("sent", não "send").
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar a forma base do verbo ("send") em vez do particípio passado ("sent") é um erro comum.

correct_answer: to prepare and issue a book, report or other written material for the public
exercises.explanation: "Publish" é tornar algo escrito disponível ao público.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. Where was the product designed?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "The new product was designed in London."
exercises.transcript: The new product was designed in London and produced in three different factories. It will be launched next spring.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "The results of the study were analysed for six months before they were published. The research was funded by a university grant." How long were the results analysed for?
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "analysed for six months".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "O relatório foi escrito ontem."
exercises.explanation: "Was written" é a forma correta da voz passiva no passado.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Esquecer o "was" ("The report written yesterday") é o erro mais comum nesta frase.

steps.content: In the passive voice, the main stress falls on the past participle, not on "was"/"were": the email was SENT, the building was BUILT — "was"/"were" stay weak and unstressed.

steps.prompt: Describe 3 things around you (an object, a building, a product) using the passive voice, focusing on the thing itself, not who made it.
Write 5 sentences in the passive voice describing facts about a product, a building or a report.
